assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: cinematic pixel-art background for PokéWorld, 16:9. Primary request: the ancient wooden tower of Ecruteak before it becomes the Burned Tower, during a violent night storm. Scene: a tall traditional five-tier Japanese timber pagoda at center, aged dark red and brown wooden beams, broad charcoal tiled roofs with curved corners, stone foundation and steps, empty old courtyard with a few maples at left and right, no modern buildings. Dramatic low-angle wide composition showing the ENTIRE tower and enough cloudy sky in the upper third for storm effects. The timber is charred in places and some roof edges broken, but its architecture is still standing. Night scene, dark navy and violet storm clouds, faint warm orange light inside broken window openings. Keep active flames and smoke OUT of the background: they will be animated separately on top of the woodwork. Detailed crisp 16-bit Pokémon Emerald-style pixel art, square color clusters and stepped outlines, cinematic layered lighting, readable silhouettes. No people, no creatures, no text, no interface, no smooth painting or blur.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: final Ho-Oh summoning cinematic background for PokéWorld, 16:9. Scene: the ceremonial summit terrace of the intact Bell Tower in Ecruteak, viewed slightly from above toward a luminous golden amber sunset. A broad ornate mahogany wooden platform fills the lower half, clear empty central floor for five separately animated kimono dancers. A short central staircase leads toward the viewer. Deep blue curved tile roofs slope down on far left and right, vermilion posts and gold railings. Two ceremonial bronze bells hang from elegant gilded supports at the rear LEFT and rear RIGHT edges of the platform, not at the center. Fine traditional Japanese woodwork, a few autumn leaves on the side roof edges. Leave the central sky from x30%-70%, y10%-58% EMPTY, no spire or hanging bell there, for a large Ho-Oh to arrive later. Large warm purple-gold clouds and distant old city roof silhouettes on the horizon. Detailed refined 16-bit Pokémon Emerald style pixel art, crisp square clusters, stepped outlines and rich but restrained palettes. No people, no Pokémon, no statues, no text or HUD, no painted blur.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: close-up sky flight background for a Ho-Oh cinematic in PokéWorld, 16:9. Scene: an expansive luminous sunset sky ABOVE a traditional Japanese tower, with layered gold, amber, rose and muted violet clouds. Clear central opening across most of the middle for a small golden light to approach the camera later. Foreground clouds at lower left and upper right create depth; a fine pale rainbow is NOT baked in, all rainbow and gold trail effects will be added in animation. No visible sun disk in the center. Magical, reverent and epic atmosphere. Detailed crisp 16-bit pixel art like Pokémon Emerald, restrained broad cloud color clusters, clear stepped edges and square pixels, no smooth airbrushing or noisy photorealistic texture. No tower, no bird, no creatures, no people, no text, no interface.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: TRANSPARENT pixel-art animation sprite sheet for five Kimono Girls dancing in a Pokémon-style Ho-Oh ceremony. Layout: exactly FIVE ROWS and FOUR COLUMNS, a regular evenly spaced grid with wide transparent margins between cells. ONE complete full-body woman in every cell, twenty sprites total. Each ROW is the SAME woman across her four dance poses, with identical size, face, clothing and palette. Row1: violet kimono with lilac obi. Row2: blue kimono with white obi. Row3: deep red kimono with gold obi. Row4: green kimono with cream obi. Row5: pink kimono with dark red obi. All are adult women in traditional floor-length patterned kimonos, dark hair in a neat Japanese bun with a small flower ornament, holding one small folding dance fan. Four COLUMNS show: 1) front-facing standing, fan held at waist; 2) left sleeve and open fan lifted gracefully outward, right arm lowered; 3) right sleeve lifted outward and open fan raised above shoulder; 4) a gentle bow with fan gathered at chest. Faces readable but simple, tasteful and dignified ceremonial choreography. Full bodies including footwear, all head tops and feet aligned within each row. Consistent orthographic front/three-quarter 2D game sprite view, NOT portraits. Crisp genuine 16-bit pixel art, stepped outlines, large clear square pixel clusters, 2-3 shades per material, no soft shading. Fully transparent background including empty grid gaps. No text, labels, grid lines, shadows, extra people or Pokémon.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the provided pixel-art pagoda scene. Change it to the SAME tower AFTER THE FIRE HAS BEEN EXTINGUISHED. Preserve exactly the camera angle, stone foundation and steps, courtyard walls, maple trees, proportions and crisp 16-bit pixel-art style. The upper four stories have collapsed: replace them with empty overcast dawn sky and a few jagged charred timber uprights. Only a blackened ground-floor shell and broken lower roof sections remain on the same foundation, with collapsed roof tiles and burned wooden beams on the platform. The former glowing window openings must now be cold and dark. The courtyard is wet. No active flames, no glowing embers, NO lightning bolts, no falling rain baked into the image. Cool gray blue dawn cloud cover fills the newly opened sky, especially the upper half, leaving space for an animated rainbow later. A little thin pale smoke above the ruins is okay. No people, no creatures, no rainbow already drawn, no text or UI. Maintain the exact square pixel clusters, stepped edges and original environment layout.
